ranking.note: Stated prerequisite for #10102, #19460 and #19461, so it cannot sit below the PRs it unblocks.
Raised five places: it is a standalone supported-platform bug fix that #32387 and #36190 both build on, so it should be looked at before them.
Raised to P2 to match #36105: both fix the shipped bitcoin wrapper failing outright on a supported platform/install layout (issue #35785).
Moved down five: it is late in the #29409→#10102 stack and cannot progress before them, and the category ranks external-software IPC reliability above wallet separation.
Moved down five: last link of the same stack, a single unique commit that only becomes reviewable after #10102 and #19460.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain, review in this order: #29409 (Chain capnp wrapper) → #10102 (multiprocess bitcoin) → #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) → #19461 (bitcoin-gui -ipcconnect). The later two each contain little unique work and are blocked until the first two land.

#32387 (ipc: windows support) states it also fixes the Windows wrapper's child exit-status tracking, which is exactly what #36105 does standalone. #36105 should be reviewed/merged first and #32387 rebased on it, to avoid duplicated work.
#36190 adds functional tests for the exit-status behaviour introduced by #36105 and is useless before it; keep them adjacent and review #36105 first.

#36105 (Windows wrapper never waits for child) and #36106 (wrapper cannot find binaries under Arch-style install dirs) are the same class of defect in the same shipped tool; they were given different bands alone and are now both P2.

#30437 (bitcoin-mine test client), #36097 (cancellation arguments) and #35671 (TxCollection) all serve the same external Stratum v2 consumer; #30437 supplies the harness used to exercise the other two, so it is the most useful entry point.
#36097 carries a temporary libmultiprocess subtree commit and #35932 depends on libmultiprocess#335; both need the upstream subtree sync decided before merge order is settled.
result.notes: The list splits cleanly: three P1s covering the core architecture plus the shutdown use-after-free, a broad P2 tier of platform fixes, external-mining interface work and the wallet/GUI separation stack, and four P3 test/build-hygiene items. #33117 is borderline for this category (it adds an interfaces::Node method primarily for GUI consumers) but it is kept at P2 because two concrete GUI PRs are waiting on it.
